findings.title: Recommendation answers lose structured provenance and cannot expose evidence citations
findings.what: The recommendation payload is allowed into Ask Claude, but evidenceRefsForAskPayload only handles session and tools views and returns an empty array for recommendations. Consequently the serialized prompt receives no evidenceRefs and the assistant message receives no clickable citations, so recommendation explanations and prioritization claims are not reproducibly tied to their source artifacts/fields.
findings.fix: Preserve each recommendation's structured provenance in the recommendation summary, derive bounded evidence references for recommendation payloads, and attach those references to both the prompt and resulting assistant message.
findings.acceptance: With ready recommendation analysis containing known provenance, send a recommendation quick prompt and assert that the outbound summary contains the expected artifact/field provenance and that the assistant response renders a citation resolving to that exact evidence.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the recommendation branch at lines 220-235 supplies recommendations, while the exhaustive evidence selector at lines 285-295 handles only sessions and tools. Lines 339-355 omit evidence when that selector is empty, and lines 455-461 therefore create an uncited assistant message. Related baseline context-building code was checked only to confirm that its recommendation projection does not restore structured provenance.

findings.title: Automation timeline creates an unbounded DOM node per run
findings.what: Although the session table is paginated, the timeline independently maps every automationTimeline.runs entry to a button. Large histories therefore create an unbounded number of DOM nodes and repeat sessionDisplay and formatting work for every run during render, increasing latency and memory use.
findings.fix: Bound the timeline surface by aggregating runs into time buckets or rendering a capped/virtualized subset while retaining access to the complete data through drill-down.
findings.acceptance: Render a dataset with at least 10,000 automation timelines and verify the timeline DOM-node count remains bounded and the render meets a documented latency/memory budget while still representing the complete run count.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the table is capped through visibleSessions at lines 319-320, but the timeline at lines 857-884 maps the complete runs array without a limit. The comparison test covers two timeline runs; its 65-session pagination fixture supplies no corresponding timelines and therefore does not exercise this path at scale.
